key_insight: Localized carrier spins in metal-halide perovskites relax through hyperfine coupling in an unusual way: electrons mainly interact with halogen nuclei, while holes are dominated by metal nuclei, and an exact dynamical model is needed in the intermediate regime.
engineering_relevance: Understanding which nuclei control spin relaxation can guide perovskite composition choices to prolong carrier spin lifetimes and improve spin-sensitive optoelectronic designs.
method: Adapted a muon spin relaxation model to localized carrier spins in perovskites.
Solved longitudinal spin relaxation exactly across arbitrary hyperfine correlation times.
Fit time-resolved Faraday rotation data to extract localization volume and correlation time.
evidence_signal: The model was applied to time-resolved Faraday rotation data from two perovskite samples and showed that a single-exponential approximation is inadequate in the experimentally relevant regime.
watch_item: The framework targets localized carriers and requires the correct correlation-time regime and material parameters, so it may not transfer directly to delocalized or strongly non-hyperfine-dominated systems.
paper_title: Hyperfine driven spin relaxation of charge carriers in metal-halide perovskites
